subject: Control plane regression during private deployment — action plan & customer update
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acmehealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@medtechsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Control plane regression during private deployment — immediate mitigation

Elena / Samir,

First, I'm sorry for the disruption this morning — we take incidents in private deployments very seriously. Around 08:35 PT we detected elevated error rates and intermittent connectivity failures for private/VPC customers that had the 2026.11.30 control-plane agent rollout in us-west-2. Some customers experienced 502/504 errors and streaming interruptions for short windows (median ~4 minutes, max ~27 minutes).

What happened (short summary):
- We introduced a minor agent+sidecar update to the private control plane at 08:10 PT that included a TLS rotation and a schema validation change.
- A configuration flag mismatch caused the control plane auth layer to reject heartbeat/handshake messages from a subset of agents, triggering degraded routing and transient failures.

Immediate mitigations we've applied:
- We paused the rollout at 08:40 PT.
- We rolled back the agent version on all affected control-plane nodes; rollback completed by 10:45 PT.
- We temporarily routed failover traffic through an isolated hosted control plane path for impacted customers while we monitored.
- We've enabled extended telemetry and log retention for impacted tenants to facilitate RCA.

Customer impact: short-lived API errors and interrupted streaming calls. We have not observed any data exfiltration or storage outside customer VPCs.

Next steps (today):
1) Share a short customer-facing incident summary and a proposed remediation timeline (attached draft).
2) Provide an RCA and postmortem once validated.
3) Schedule a technical sync with your infra/ops team to walk the timeline and controls.

Attachments: redwood_postmortem_draft_v1.pdf (draft), config-diff-20261130.txt (changed flags), screenshot-ctrlplane-error.png (example 502 trace).

I'll be on the call if you'd like to sync — propose 11:30 PT today; if that doesn't work we'll find an alternative.

Again, apologies for the disruption.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
Dylan.Brooks@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Date: 2026-11-30T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Control plane regression during private deployment — immediate mitigation

Thanks, Dylan.

We appreciate the prompt rollback and the note. A couple quick questions from our side:
- Please confirm whether any telemetry/logs or control-plane state was written to Redwood-managed storage outside our VPC during the incident. Our security team needs that explicitly.
- Will you be sharing a timeline that includes when the problematic agent rolled out to our nodes and when rollback completed? We need that for our change audit.
- What's your estimate for a final RCA and whether there will be any billing credit given the outage window (it affected a few of our nightly batch jobs).

We can do 11:30 PT if you want to walk this through.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Health
elena.ruiz@acmehealth.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acmehealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@medtechsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T12:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Control plane regression during private deployment — action plan and draft RCA

Hi Elena — quick answers and a slightly expanded timeline below. Thanks for the questions.

Direct answers:
- Data residency: No telemetry or control-plane state was written to any Redwood-managed persistent storage outside your VPC. All logs and traces collected for debugging were captured from in-VPC agents and retained only per your configured retention window. We have not pushed any customer data to an external bucket.
- Timeline (high level):
  - 08:10 PT: rollout of agent v2026.11.30 started for private control plane nodes in us-west-2.
  - 08:35 PT: monitoring alert for elevated 502/504 rates and increased reconnects.
  - 08:40 PT: rollout paused and mitigation playbook invoked.
  - 08:50–10:45 PT: stepwise rollback across control-plane nodes; majority recovered by 09:20, final nodes completed by 10:45.
  - 11:00 PT: monitoring window confirmed stability.
- RCA (summary): Root cause is a schema/flag mismatch triggered during the TLS rotation. A config flag (allow-unverified-agent) defaulted to false in the new agent image for certain environments; combined with a timing window during cert rotation, a subset of agent handshakes were rejected by the control-plane auth validation. That rejection resulted in transient routing failures.

Remediation and prevention:
- We have reverted the default flag behavior and added a gated preflight check for agent-controlplane compatibility.
- We will add a canary stage to private control-plane rollouts that also validates agent heartbeat acceptance and auth handshake success before broad rollout.
- We will expand our post-rollback monitoring to capture early signal thresholds and alert on handshake rejections specifically.

On credits: We don't auto-apply credits for short transient windows. Given the impact to your nightly jobs, I'm marking this for manager review and will propose a discretionary credit. Marissa (CC) will coordinate next steps.

I've attached the current draft of the postmortem for your review (redwood_postmortem_draft_v1.pdf) and the config diff we used to validate the issue. If you'd like a deeper technical session, we can book a follow-up with our runtime eng team.

Proposed next steps:
- 11:30 PT call to walk this (I will join; runtime and delivery on call).
- Finalize postmortem and share within 48 hours.
- Provide formal credit decision within 72 hours.

— Dylan
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T16:47:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Acme Health incident — credit request and next steps

Team,

Summary: Private control-plane rollout v2026.11.30 caused transient auth/handshake rejections for a subset of agents (us-west-2). Rollback completed by 10:45 PT; no data left the customer VPCs. Customer (Acme) is asking for RCA and potential credit for impacted nightly batch jobs.

Asks:
- Marissa: can you approve a discretionary credit proposal (initial suggestion: 10% off November consumption) so I can give Elena a firm commitment during follow-up? If legal needs to review, loop them in.
- Karthik: please confirm the change in agent defaults and the canary rollout gating so I can include the specific remediation items in the final postmortem. Include a target ETA for the gating change (ETA requested: 2026-12-07).
- Laura: heads-up in case Acme escalates to sales/GTM — they may request an executive readout. If that happens, I'll coordinate a short summary.

Related items: postmortem draft in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/PM-ACME-042; HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-4321.

I'll prepare the customer-facing RCA and the credit proposal once Marissa confirms the credit band.

Thanks,
Dylan
